page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with a reduced memory-to-vCPU allocation, optimized for scale-out compute and high I/O throughput. Powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor, the instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without multithreading overhead. Memory capacity is set at 64.0 GB (2.0 GB per vCPU), supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage, though it contains zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel execution and memory subsystem throughput. In multi-core tests, the server placed in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 66,296.43 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,774.0, while single-core performance remained average at 1,656.0. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated top-tier performance (top 10%), recording 450.77 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 169.21 GB/sec for write operations. Similarly, PassMark database operations achieved a top-tier score of 37,222.49, complemented by strong Redis SET throughput of 61.98 million operations per second and 53.68 GB/sec in static web serving.

Hardware tradeoffs focus primarily on the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and instruction support. Because the arm64 architecture lacks x86 vector sets like AVX-512, workloads reliant on Intel or AMD extensions are unsupported. Furthermore, large-model CPU inference underperforms, registering in the bottom 10% for 70B model prompt processing (4.66 tokens/sec). Conversely, qualitative cost efficiency is solid for high-concurrency tasks due to dense dedicated core counts and rapid integrated NVMe storage.

This hardware balance makes Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 optimal for multi-threaded build systems, CI/CD pipelines, high-throughput static web serving, caching tiers, and distributed database nodes that leverage local NVMe storage without requiring extensive memory overhead.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory ARM instance powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with 64.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and includes 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. While lacking hardware GPUs and x86 instruction sets like AVX-512, the system excels in parallel processing and data movement. Benchmark highlights include top-tier memory bandwidth (450.77 GB/sec uncached read) and top-tier PassMark database operations (37,222.49), alongside strong multi-core compute in stress-ng (66,296.43) and Redis SET throughput (61.98 million ops/sec). Single-core execution and large-parameter LLM inference are comparatively moderate. Given its balanced 1:2 memory ratio and bundled NVMe disk, the instance delivers high compute efficiency for distributed databases, caching systems, CI/CD compilation, and high-concurrency web tiers.
